title: The counter and money handling
summary: Money in TCG Card Shop Simulator changes hands at the counter: the game treats a cash change as an interaction with its own currency data and its own counter settings.
body: Handing over change is an interaction in the world rather than a silent arithmetic step, which is why the counter is somewhere you stand.
Currency data has its own place in that system, so the money you handle is defined rather than drawn from a fixed number.
The counter keeps settings of its own, which is why a busy counter can be configured instead of merely being staffed.
What this entry does not tell you: exchange rates, how much change is available or how a mistake affects a customer. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A cash change at the counter is its own interaction.
Currency is defined as data in the game.
The counter has its own settings screen.
The game ships a counter sign of its own for a counter that is closed.
The till has its own drawer objects for opening and closing, and the counter keeps its money guides as a group.
The checkout register has an open state of its own, with a sound effect for it.
Pressing a card at the counter and finishing the sale each have a sound of their own.
Scanning an item, opening the register and finalising a card each have a sound of their own, several of them with a pad version beside them.
facts.evidence: asset names: SFX_CheckoutScan, SFX_CheckoutScan_Pad, SFX_CheckoutRegisterOpen_Pad, SFX_FinalizeCard

facts.claim: A customer buying, a declined payment and a damaged card each have a sound of their own.
